justification: All five round-1 findings are fixed and verified verbatim against the live sources, fetched directly, not from memory or cache: (1) line ~509's nvie.com quote now reads 'it "allow[s] for minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release," while "adding large new features here is strictly prohibited"' -- both fragments match nvie.com's live text exactly ('Furthermore, they allow for minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release (version number, build dates, etc.)' and 'Adding large new features here is strictly prohibited. They must be merged into develop...'); the bracketed [s] correctly marks the verb-tense change for embedding in the article's own sentence. (2) line ~236's git-tag quote now reads 'annotated tags are meant for release while lightweight tags are meant for private or temporary object labels' -- this is the live page's DESCRIPTION-section sentence verbatim (source capitalizes 'Annotated' since it opens a sentence there; the article lowercases it because the quote is embedded mid-sentence, which is normal practice, not an alteration). (3) line ~119's trunk-based-development quote now reads 'use feature flags in day to day development to allow for hedging on the order of releases' -- matches the live page verbatim. (4) line ~696's Conventional Commits quote now reads 'regardless of type' -- matches the FAQ's 'Commits with BREAKING CHANGE in the commits, regardless of type, should be translated to MAJOR' verbatim. (5) line ~224's semver quote now reads 'the public API SHOULD NOT be considered stable' with 'public' restored -- matches semver.org section 4 verbatim. I did not stop at the five flagged spots: I fetched all five sources plus git-scm.com/docs/git-tag, docs.github.com/.../github-flow and docs.github.com/.../about-pull-request-merges a second time each and checked every other quoted fragment in the article against live page text -- the master/develop HEAD-state quotes, the '--no-ff... a few more (empty) commit objects' quote, the hotfix 'very much like release branches... albeit unplanned' quote, the 2020-note quotes about 'multiple versions of the software running in the wild' and 'a much simpler workflow (like GitHub flow)', the six GitHub-flow step names, the draft-PR and branch-protection and delete-your-branch quotes, the merge-commit and squash-merge descriptions, and the feat/fix MUST rules and the '!'/footer breaking-change rules -- all match verbatim. I found one new, minor issue not previously flagged (below): a stray ellipsis in the opening Trunk-Based Development quote implies an elision that is not actually present in the source. It is a quoting-mechanics nit, not a misrepresentation -- the omitted clause changes no meaning -- so I have not treated it as a second capping factual error alongside a fixed round; it is the only outstanding sourcing issue on the page. Separately, I independently rebuilt both affected repositories (storefront, ticketing) completely from scratch outside the harness, in a fresh scratch directory, using the exact commands printed in the article and the same pinned identity (Ada Example / ada@example.com) and dates (GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-15T10:00:00Z) as round 1. Every commit hash, deleted-branch line, tag listing and log line in both edited panels -- the storefront 'discounts flag' panel (fb7d5a7, 0162249, 0231e49, and everything built on top of it: c4ae26e, 9a8e1dd, 2b9a5d6, a9efec3, ea4e212) and the ticketing 'row count' hotfix panel (1f19068, 8638ade, 5a7eca4, 933f0f4, a08d0a2, 8006add, c37e574, fcf1bf3, faf0c75, bc59002, c5414f7) -- matched the article byte for byte in my independent replay, confirming the regeneration was a real re-run and not a hand-edited hash. I also re-verified, independently, the one non-obvious downstream claim that a shortened commit subject could plausibly have desynced: 'four merges into main and five more into develop.' `git rev-list --count --merges main` on my from-scratch replay gives 4, and `git rev-list --count --merges develop` gives 5 (the fifth being the main-side release-1.0.0 merge riding onto develop via the hotfix branch, the same non-obvious mechanism round 1 found) -- the claim survives the edit exactly. `node tools/run-code.mjs src/content/articles/version-control/git-workflows.md` passed 3/3 consecutive runs in this worktree, always `PASS ... blocks=36 executed=18`, matching round 1 with no flakiness. The prior round's other strengths stand unchanged on a fresh read: no filler, five varied exercises with solutions that don't leak output early, a comparison table that earns its place (now with shorter cells that still say the same thing), and correct complexity/mechanism claims throughout (annotated vs. lightweight tags, `-d` vs `-D`'s merge check, squash merges being single-parent, `%s` vs `%B` in git log format strings). The design-driven changes bundled into this round (SVG id renames to avoid a TBD-substring false positive, the shortened table cells, and the resized release-0.2 box in Figure 1) do not touch any technical claim and remain internally consistent (aria-labelledby ids, marker ids and their references all still match). With no remaining fabricated or misattributed quote and no misrepresentation of any cited source, this article is now deeper and more rigorously fact-checked than any of the compared existing pages (Atlassian's guide and GitHub's own docs do not execute or verify anything, and nvie's post only covers Git Flow), which clears the 8.5 'equal to the best existing result' anchor; it is held short of a 9.5+ score only by the one trivial stray-ellipsis nit below.

issues.location: Line 56 (Trunk-Based Development section): '"developers collaborate on code in a single branch called \'trunk\' ... and resist any pressure to create other long-lived development branches."'
issues.problem: The live page at https://trunkbaseddevelopment.com/ has no gap between "single branch called 'trunk'" and "and resist any pressure..." -- the full sentence is 'A source-control branching model, where developers collaborate on code in a single branch called 'trunk' and resist any pressure to create other long-lived development branches by employing documented techniques.' There is nothing omitted between those two clauses, so the mid-quote ellipsis implies an elision that did not happen. (The article separately, and unmarked, drops the trailing 'by employing documented techniques' -- that is standard, unproblematic trailing truncation and not part of this finding.) This does not change what the source is claiming, so it is not a misrepresentation, but it is not a verbatim-accurate use of an ellipsis.
issues.fixLooksLike: Replace the mid-quote '...' with a space (or an em dash outside the quotation marks) since nothing was actually cut there: "developers collaborate on code in a single branch called 'trunk' and resist any pressure to create other long-lived development branches."
